name: Nathan
overview: Nathan was a male member of the tribe of Judah, uniquely identified as a son of King David. His role and significance are rooted in his royal lineage and his involvement in the Davidic dynasty. No additional personal notes are recorded beyond his familial connections.
namesAndTitles: The name Nathan means 'gift' in Hebrew. It is a proper name given to him, though not directly by God, reflecting a common biblical name without additional titles or meanings noted.
familyAndRelationships: Nathan is explicitly recorded as a son of David and Bathsheba, establishing his direct royal descent. He is also inferred to be the father of Mattatha, linking him to subsequent generations. These relationships underscore his place within the Davidic line.
scriptureSignificance: Nathan's importance in Scripture stems from his position within the royal family of Judah as David's son. He is associated with the fulfillment of God's covenant promises to David, particularly concerning the eternal dynasty. His lineage and prophetic connections highlight God's faithfulness in preserving the Davidic line and preparing for Solomon's reign.
